text:
Samir Gupta: Heads-up from today's chaos run: during sustained ingress pressure we saw a cluster of opaque 502s and aggressive client retries. Hard to tell whether clients retried incorrectly or our proxy returned the wrong semantic codes.
Priya Nair: Can you share the minimal repro? was this streaming reads or strict request/response?
Samir Gupta: Repro was streaming generation (/v1/stream) with artificial token refill throttle. After ~60s of backpressure some sessions aborted and clients retried, producing higher upstream load. Log example: ```[edge-n9] 2026-03-26T14:22:01Z POST /v1/stream conn=sess-7a8 upstream=running proxy_abort=client_reset status=502```
Ben Holt: Oof. We currently collapse client_reset, upstream_timeout, and internal_queue_drop into 5xx. That makes retry rules noisy.
Dana Kim: Short term fix: stop using 502 for client-initiated aborts. Map client disconnect -> 499, upstream timeout -> 504, ingress-queue-drop -> 429. That should reduce accidental client-side retry storms.
Priya Nair: Agreed. Also we should add a small header to the abort path: X-Edge-Abort-Reason: client_disconnect|upstream_timeout|ingress_overload so observability and customers can know what happened.
Samir Gupta: Medium term idea: instead of immediate hard abort, offer a streaming reset handshake. Return a 4xx with X-Resume-Offer header with a resume token and allow clients to reconnect and continue from last acked token. This reduces full restarts and duplicate upstream work.
Ben Holt: Implementation notes: per-node resumestore (sharded) holding compact resume entries: {upstream_checkpoint, kv_offset, ttl, tenant_id, hmac}. Token = base64(header.payload.signature). Must HMAC with rotating node key.
Dana Kim: We must be conservative: resume only for idempotent or side-effect-safe endpoints, or when the upstream provides a checkpoint/commit id. Otherwise reject resume attempts.
Priya Nair: Token validation pseudocode: ```decode token; verify hmac & keyid; check ttl; if payload.tenant != request.tenant reject; if payload.upstream_checkpoint != current_upstream_checkpoint then reject (unless endpoint is idempotent)```
Samir Gupta: Metrics we need: resume_offers, resume_accepts, resume_rejects{stale,capacity,non_idempotent}, resumestore_entries, resumestore_bytes, resumestore_evictions. Alert if resume_rejects/stores grow rapidly.
Ben Holt: Resources: estimate 200 bytes per resume entry * 25k entries/node = ~5MB. CPU to GC shards could be a concern; propose 16 shards/node by default to spread locks.
Dana Kim: Hedging interaction: if a resume is accepted we MUST avoid hedging or duplicate upstream calls. The node must surface an upstream-commit-id in the token and ensure no concurrent hedges while resume is being applied.
Priya Nair: Security: include key-id, and support key rotation. Offer a grace window where old keys can validate tokens for X minutes. Also include nonce to prevent replay across restarts.
Samir Gupta: Rollout plan: 1) next sprint: error-class split + X-Edge-Abort-Reason header. 2) follow-up sprint: feature-flagged resume-offer on canary nodes (Dedicated clusters first). 3) If stable, roll to hosted.
Ben Holt: Action items: Ben -> PR for error mapping + header. Dana -> design doc for resumestore (proto, sharding, eviction). Priya -> telemetry dashboard mock and alerts. Samir -> update chaos harness to exercise resume flow.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: edge-release v3.0.1-canary to prod-canary at 2026-03-28T06:00Z. Watch: 499 ratio, resume_offers (should be 0 until FF enabled), 502 trend.
Priya Nair: One more: billing implications. If client resumes and we avoid re-generation, billing records need to reflect resumed consumption. I'll loop in billing to confirm how we log token usage across resumes.
Dana Kim: Also document client-side flow: if client gets X-Resume-Offer, it should POST /v1/resume with header X-Resume-Token and include Idempotency-Key when applicable. Server responds 200 + streaming continuation or 410 if token expired.
Ben Holt: I'll include unit tests and an e2e in the PR to ensure we don't accidentally allow resume on non-idempotent endpoints.
Samir Gupta: Great. Let's keep this channel for followups. Drop architecture questions here before we start the design doc. :thumbsup:
